findings.title: Flagged table widgets render with empty columns and data
findings.body: When `use-table-widget-visualization` is enabled, `tableResultComponent` swaps the real table for `TableWidgetVisualization` with `columns={[]}` and `tableData` hardcoded to `{data: [], meta: {fields: {}, units: {}}}`. `columns ?? fallback` does not treat `[]` as missing, so columns are not derived from meta either. Query results, loading state, field headers, and custom cell renderers are all dropped, so every dashboard table widget for that org renders blank.

findings.title: Error payloads are paired by dict order, not event id
findings.body: `fetch_error_details` builds nodestore ids from `error_ids`, then does `zip(error_ids, events.values())`. `get_multi` returns a dict keyed by node id and omits missing keys; value order is not the request order. A missing or reordered event attaches another event's title, message, and timestamp to the wrong id and drops the last id, so the Seer summary describes the wrong errors. Index with `events.get(node_id)` per id. The new test only stores one present event, so it does not catch this.

findings.title: Unnormalized error timestamps crash or mis-order summaries
findings.body: Error context defaults on. Timestamps from nodestore are stored raw and then compared with `<` to each segment event's numeric `timestamp` (default 0) while merging logs. Ingested events persist `timestamp` as an ISO-8601 string; `str < float` raises TypeError outside `fetch_error_details`'s try/except, so any replay with error ids 500s the summarize endpoint instead of returning a summary. The new test passes a float into `store_event`, so it does not lock the production shape. Segment fixtures in this same file use small offsets like `0.0` while event timestamps are unix time, so even two numbers will not interleave. Coerce both sides to one numeric unit before sort/compare.

findings.title: Error ids depend on the client's field allowlist
findings.body: The endpoint always runs `process_raw_response(..., fields=request.query_params.getlist("field"))` and then reads `error_ids` from that projection. The replay AI tab calls this URL with no `field` param, and any caller that passes `field` for something else will not include `error_ids`. If that helper only emits requested keys, error context is silently empty in the UI this change is for. The new test also omits `field` while expecting exception text in the Seer body, so it only passes if an empty field list means "all fields". Force `error_ids` into the internal lookup instead of forwarding the client field list.

findings.title: Each segment page is summarized with every remaining error
findings.body: `error_events` is closed over the paginator `on_results` callback, but `gen_request_data` flushes every not-yet-emitted error after the current page's segments. `GenericOffsetPaginator` only supplies one page (a long replay is many more than one page of segments). The first page, which is all the AI tab loads, therefore appends later errors instead of interleaving them with later breadcrumbs, and later pages repeat those errors in their Seer requests. Only emit errors whose timestamps fall in the page being summarized.

findings.title: Unescaped issue titles break or inject PR comment links
findings.body: `MERGED_PR_SINGLE_ISSUE_TEMPLATE` puts the issue title inside a markdown link (`[**{title}**]({url})`) after only truncating to 50 characters. Titles often contain `]`. That character closes the link early, so the GitHub/GitLab suspect-issue comment points at the wrong URL. A title an attacker can set by sending an error, such as `Click me](https://evil.example)`, injects an arbitrary link into the bot comment developers read on the PR. Escape `]` (and other markdown link characters) before formatting.

findings.title: Report validation rejects real browser URLs and ignores age 0
findings.body: `url` is a DRF `URLField`, which only allows http(s)/ftp(s). Reporting API document URLs are often `about:blank`, `chrome-extension:`, or other non-http schemes. Those reports now 422 the entire batch; the previous dataclass accepted any string. `validate_timestamp` / `validate_age` also use `initial_data.get("age")` and `get("timestamp")`, which are falsy for 0, so a spec-valid `age: 0` combined with a timestamp skips the mutual-exclusion error (and the reverse). Allow the schemes browsers actually send, and test key presence rather than truthiness.

findings.title: Hidden span attributes are still shown until the user searches
findings.body: `HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES` (`is_segment`, `project_id`, `received`) is applied only in the search branch. An empty `searchQuery` returns `sortAttributes(attributes)` immediately, so those fields remain in the default attributes panel. The hide filter has to run before that early return; otherwise the new constant never affects the view users actually see.

findings.title: Feedback summary ignores the environment page filter
findings.body: The summary request sends only the normalized datetime and `selection.projects`. The list page is under `PageFiltersContainer`, so the feedback list is environment-scoped, but this query never sends `selection.environments` (or the active feedback search). With an environment selected, the summary above the list describes feedback from other environments than the rows the user is looking at.

findings.title: 60s auth-check deadline skips SSO refresh after last_synced is bumped
findings.body: `check_auth_identities` now has `processing_deadline_duration=60` and previously had none. It walks up to `chunk_size` (default 100) identities, each doing an organization RPC plus `provider.refresh_identity` HTTP. If the worker is killed at 60s, the trailing `check_auth.apply_async` that continues the chain never runs. `check_auth` already set `last_synced=now` for the whole id list before enqueue, so those identities are not selected again for about a day and their SSO validity is not refreshed. Raise the deadline to fit the batch, or set `last_synced` only after a successful check.

findings.title: AI summary errors while the project list is still loading
findings.body: The new guard treats `replayRecord.project_id && !project` as "Project not found". `useProjectFromId` is also undefined while the project store is still loading, not only when the id is missing. The first render shows an error alert and keeps the summarize query disabled (`project?.slug` is missing) until projects arrive, instead of the loading state. Only show that error after the project list has finished loading.

findings.title: Trace waterfall wrapper lost height 100%
findings.body: The waterfall root changed from a flex column with `flex-grow: 1` and `height: 100%` to `<Flex direction="column" flex={1}>`. `flex={1}` does not set height. If the parent lays this view out by height rather than as a stretched flex item, the waterfall no longer fills the trace viewer and scrolling breaks. Put an explicit `height`/`min-height: 100%` back on that container.
